The Unreal Past: I'd rather ... / It's time ...
You use I'd rather ... or It's time ... when you talk about a situation that you would like to change or an action you would like someone to take.

I'd rather and It's time are followed by the Unreal Past. The verb is in the past, but the situation is in the present. You use I'd rather when you talk about a course of action you would prefer someone to take.

Structure:
I'd rather/ It's time + subject pronoun + Past Simple

Example:
I'd rather they went home.
It's time your bosses did their fair share of the work.
Well, I'd rather I talked to a professional for career advice than ask my dad.
They'd rather did all the work while they played golf.
I'd rather we went to the movies than stay at home.
It's time your parents gave you more freedom.
It's time you delegated a little more.
It was time she created a more acceptable work-life balance.
You use time clauses to link different clauses and events. Usually, a time clause introduces a subordinate clause in relation to another event found in the main clause.
You use words like as or strong and while to talk about consecutive actions or to talk about an action taking place almost at the same time or immediately after something else happens.

You use as when you want to say that something happens almost at the same time as another event starts. You often add just to the time clause.
Example:
Just as I started my shift, I realized I left my phone at home.

You use when to talk about things that happened immediately after another event.
Example:
When she finished lunch, she went out for a walk and discovered that she could barely get down the street.
We met while she was working downtown.
When she finished her shift at the pub, she would then go out with colleagues to all hours of the night.
One day, when she finished lunch, she went for a walk and discovered she could barely get down the street.
Just as she finished her work day, she felt her health deteriorating.

You use while to talk about two longer actions happening at the same time.
Example:
While she was working there, she felt her health was deteriorating.
to all hours of the night
Example: She would then go out with colleagues to all hours of the night.

Amy: What we do here is help people move forward and set personal and professional goals that will give them the life they really want. Most life coaching clients are healthy, successful people who might be a bit stuck or simply want to make a big change in their lives and want the support of their own personal coach to do so.
Vanessa: Well, I'd rather I talked to a professional for career advice than ask my dad.
Amy: I worked with another person who was in the pub business and together we made some real progress.
Vanessa: Oh? What was her story?

Amy: Well, we met while she was working downtown. When she finished her shift at the pub, she would then go out with colleagues to all hours of the night. While she was working there, she felt her health was deteriorating. One day, when she finished lunch, she went for a walk and discovered she could barely get down the street. When she couldn't breathe properly, she finally contacted me and that's when we concluded that it was time she created a more acceptable work-life balance.
Vanessa: Ok, that sounds very familiar to my situation. I have a lot of stress at work. I run everything. The owners are never there. They'd rather I did all the work while they played golf. I also take on too much responsibility. I often stay late and let my staff go home early. I'd rather they went home and chill out than stay and work late.

Amy: Well off the top of my head, I'd say it's time your bosses did their fair share and it's time you delegated a little more.
Vanessa: Yeah, but how?
Amy: We'll go over that later. Now Vanessa, I have a little homework for you.
Vanessa: What is it?
Amy: It's a life balance wheel.
